summary: Closed the last unobserved half of the main account: whether the stale membership view survives a later configuration change. The two-mode cluster harness now, after the long run, puts a current-configuration node in charge, adds voter F through the normal AddVoter path, and samples again. Local construction feedback shows the split precisely: the new configuration entry is processed normally by the restarted node, so its view becomes {A,B,C,D,E,F} in both modes, while in the feature-on run the entry at the conflict index remains different across nodes and the restarted node's FSM still holds the write only its own side accepted, whereas the feature-off control stays consistent and its FSM holds the majority write. That bounds the stale membership to the interval before the next membership change while showing the entry and applied divergence is untouched by it. The experiment is filed as a revision of the child question's previous experiment (same investigation) with five comparisons over the new 'reconfigured' event in both modes, a structural admission and the new phase described in the scope and prefix. Incomplete: that receipt and its interpretation, the user Restore and term-changing truncation repair paths, and the operational frequency of the fall-behind that triggers the snapshot repair.
